items.title: George "Kid Sheik" Colar Interview, 1958-07-20
items.q: a fella was amazed to me on trombone was Harrison Bradley. Harrison Bradley.

ctx.x: So we've had a few trumpet players you mentioned, a few clarinet players, and what about trombone players, who stuck in your mind as being truly remarkable?

Well, I mean, during the time back, uh, what I remember, and the trombone players I was around, and, uh, I'll tell you, out all of them, I mean, uh, uh, uh, uh, uh, a fella was amazed to me on trombone was Harrison Bradley. Harrison Bradley. And he worked at Brinn-Renné for years and all, but he was, I mean, really, a good trombone player. He had everything it take to be a trombone player. I mean, he had every technique, tone, anything. I mean, he never did get excited on it and all. He was just right there.…

Yeah, he played it as an inch. Talking about Kid Renné, what was in, in those days when his lip was real hard and all that, when he was really in his heyday, what was his strongest point, what was his specialty?
